title: What Are Idioms, Euphemisms, and Slang? (And Should You Learn Them?)
speaker: Tom Wilkinson

keywords.def: A group of words whose meaning is different from the meanings of the individual words.
A polite or indirect word used to avoid saying something unpleasant or rude.
Very informal words or expressions used by particular groups, often changing quickly over time.
Taking words in their most basic and exact meaning, not using imagination or symbolism.
Using language in a creative or symbolic way, not with its normal or literal meaning.
Showing respect and good manners when speaking or behaving.
Relaxed and casual in style; not suitable for serious or official situations.

sentences.en: Have you ever heard someone say, “kick the bucket” or “pass away,” and felt confused?
sentences.zh: 你有没有听过别人说“kick the bucket”或“pass away”，然后感到很困惑？

sentences.en: They both have the meaning of “die”… but are used in different contexts.
sentences.zh: 它们都有“死”的意思……但在不同的语境下使用。

sentences.en: English, like all languages, is full of phrases and expressions that don’t always make sense if you look at the words literally.
sentences.zh: 英语和所有语言一样，充满了各种短语和表达，如果你从字面意思上去理解，往往说不通。

sentences.en: Native speakers use this kind of language all the time… in conversations, TV shows, songs, and workplaces.
sentences.zh: 母语者经常使用这种语言……在日常对话、电视剧、歌曲和职场中。

sentences.en: But for English learners, idiomatic and informal expressions can be some of the hardest parts of the language to understand.
sentences.zh: 但对于英语学习者来说，习语和非正式表达可能是最难理解的部分之一。

sentences.en: In today’s episode, we’re going to explore idioms, euphemisms, and slang.
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目中，我们将探讨习语、委婉语和俚语。

sentences.en: These are three important (and sometimes confusing) types of everyday English.
sentences.zh: 这三种是日常英语中很重要（有时也令人困惑）的语言类型。

sentences.en: We’ll talk about what they mean, why native speakers use them, and whether you should spend time learning and using them yourself.
sentences.zh: 我们将讨论它们的含义、母语者为什么使用它们，以及你是否应该花时间自己去学习和使用它们。

sentences.en: By the end of this episode, you’ll have a clearer idea of how these kinds of expressions work and how understanding them can help you sound more natural and follow native-level conversations more easily.
sentences.zh: 听完这期节目后，你会对这些表达的工作原理有一个更清晰的认识，并且明白理解它们如何能帮助你听起来更地道，更轻松地跟上母语级别的对话。

sentences.en: Let’s start with idiomatic language. Idioms are probably one of the more frustrating parts of language learning.
sentences.zh: 让我们从习语开始。习语可以说是语言学习中最让人沮丧的部分之一。

sentences.en: They are also a big part of the online English education and English content creation world.
sentences.zh: 它们也是在线英语教育和英语内容创作世界中的一个重头戏。

sentences.en: There are millions of videos or podcasts online introducing lists of idioms for English learners.
sentences.zh: 网上有数百万个视频或播客，专门为英语学习者介绍各种习语列表。

sentences.en: Some of these videos are useful, many of them are not.
sentences.zh: 其中一些视频很有用，但很多并没有什么用。

sentences.en: But what actually is an idiom? And what do they do?
sentences.zh: 但习语到底是什么？它们有什么作用？

sentences.en: An idiom is a phrase or expression whose meaning is different from the literal meaning of the words.
sentences.zh: 习语是一个短语或表达，其含义与字面意思不同。

sentences.en: For example, when someone says “break the ice “, they don’t mean physically breaking ice.
sentences.zh: 例如，当有人说“break the ice”时，他们并不是指物理上去破冰。

sentences.en: They mean starting a conversation or making people feel more comfortable in a social situation.
sentences.zh: 他们的意思是打破僵局，或者让人们在社交场合中感到更自在。

sentences.en: Similarly, “spill the beans” doesn’t involve beans at all.
sentences.zh: 同样，“spill the beans”和豆子一点关系也没有。

sentences.en: It means to reveal a secret. And if something is a “blessing in disguise “, it might seem bad at first, but it actually leads to something good.
sentences.zh: 它的意思是泄露秘密。如果某事是“blessing in disguise”，它一开始可能看起来是件坏事，但实际上会带来好结果。

sentences.en: Idioms are everywhere in English and other languages too.
sentences.zh: 习语在英语和其他语言中随处可见。

sentences.en: We use them in everyday conversations, books, news, movies, and songs.
sentences.zh: 我们在日常对话、书籍、新闻、电影和歌曲中都会使用它们。

sentences.en: They help speakers express complex ideas in short and perhaps more emotional ways.
sentences.zh: 它们帮助说话者用简短甚至更有表现力的方式表达复杂的想法。

sentences.en: Instead of describing every detail, an idiom gives meaning through imagery, emotion, and shared understanding.
sentences.zh: 习语不是去描述每一个细节，而是通过意象、情感和共同理解来传达含义。

sentences.en: But that’s also what makes idioms really tricky for non-native speakers and learners.
sentences.zh: 但这也是为什么习语对非母语者和学习者来说非常棘手的原因。

sentences.en: They’re tricky because they are deeply connected to culture and history.
sentences.zh: 它们很棘手，因为它们与文化和历史紧密相连。

sentences.en: You can’t always, or really you can never, translate them word for word.
sentences.zh: 你不能总是——或者说实际上你永远不能——逐字翻译它们。

sentences.en: They may have developed from a very specific historical or cultural origin.
sentences.zh: 它们可能是从非常特殊的历史或文化渊源中发展而来的。

sentences.en: And if you are not familiar with that history or you are not from that specific culture, it will be almost impossible to guess the meaning of an idiom.
sentences.zh: 如果你不熟悉这段历史，或者不来自那种特定的文化，你几乎不可能猜出一个习语的意思。

sentences.en: We can clearly see this when we compare idioms with similar meanings from a variety of different languages.
sentences.zh: 当我们把不同语言中含义相似的习语进行比较时，这一点就非常明显了。

sentences.en: For example, in English the idiom “too many cooks spoil the broth” means if too many people are involved in a task or activity, it will not be done well.
sentences.zh: 例如，在英语中，“too many cooks spoil the broth”这个习语的意思是，如果太多人参与一项任务或活动，这件事就做不好。

sentences.en: In other languages, the equivalent idiom is very different.
sentences.zh: 在其他语言中，对应的习语非常不同。

sentences.en: “Many midwives… child will be lazy” in Croatian.
sentences.zh: 克罗地亚语里是：“助产士太多……孩子就会变懒”。

sentences.en: “Many pigs make the slop sparse” in Dutch.
sentences.zh: 荷兰语里是：“猪多泔水少”。

sentences.en: “A child looked after by seven nannies is without one eye” in Russian.
sentences.zh: 俄语里是：“七个保姆照顾的孩子没有一只眼睛”。

sentences.en: I found these idioms from a list published by the European Day of Languages celebration.
sentences.zh: 这些习语是我从欧洲语言日庆祝活动发布的一个列表中找到的。

sentences.en: So I hope they are real idioms, but correct me if I’m wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望它们是真正的习语，如果我弄错了请纠正我。

sentences.en: Idioms reflect how people in a culture think and they change depending on what images people find natural and what metaphors they use to describe life.
sentences.zh: 习语反映了一个文化中人们的思维方式，它们会随着人们觉得自然的意象以及用来描述生活的隐喻而改变。

sentences.en: This is obvious when you think about some of the differences between idioms used in different dialects of English as well.
sentences.zh: 当你思考英语不同方言所使用的习语之间的一些差异时，这一点就很明显了。

sentences.en: In British English, we “take something with a pinch of salt” while in the US you “take something with a grain of salt” (both meaning to think twice before you believe it).
sentences.zh: 在英式英语中，我们说“take something with a pinch of salt”，而在美国，你则说“take something with a grain of salt”（两者意思都是在相信之前要三思）。

sentences.en: Or in the UK we would say “jump the queue” when someone unfairly goes in front of us while waiting in line.
sentences.zh: 或者在英国，当有人在排队时插队，我们会说“jump the queue”。

sentences.en: Or “do the washing up” when we are washing dishes.
sentences.zh: 或者当我们洗碗时，我们会说“do the washing up”。

sentences.en: But in US English, it isn’t really that common to use this vocabulary, so the idioms are different too.
sentences.zh: 但在美式英语中，使用这种词汇并不太常见，所以习语也不同。

sentences.en: “Cut in line” or “do the dishes”. In summary, idioms add some humor and emotion to our speech.
sentences.zh: “Cut in line”或“do the dishes”。总之，习语为我们的演讲增添了一些幽默感和情感。

sentences.en: Native speakers use them to sound more expressive and natural, and as a learner, recognizing idioms can help you understand the way English speakers think and communicate.
sentences.zh: 母语者使用它们来让自己的表达更有表现力、更地道；而作为学习者，识别习语可以帮助你理解英语使用者的思维和交流方式。

sentences.en: Now let’s move on to euphemisms. Euphemisms are another type of indirect or figurative language that you’ll hear all the time.
sentences.zh: 接下来我们来看看委婉语。委婉语是你经常会听到的另一种间接或比喻性的语言。

sentences.en: A euphemism is a polite or indirect word or phrase used to replace something that might sound unpleasant, embarrassing, or offensive.
sentences.zh: 委婉语是一种礼貌或间接的词语或短语，用来替代那些听起来可能令人不快、尴尬或冒犯的说法。

sentences.en: For example, instead of saying someone “died”, people often say they “passed away”.
sentences.zh: 例如，人们不说某人“died（死）”，而经常说他们“passed away（离世）”。

sentences.en: Instead of saying an employee was “fired”, a company might say they were “let go”.
sentences.zh: 公司不说员工被“fired（开除）”，可能会说他们被“let go（优化/裁掉）”。

sentences.en: And rather than calling someone “old”, people might say “senior citizen” or “elderly “.
sentences.zh: 人们不说某人“old（老）”，而可能会说“senior citizen（老年公民）”或“elderly（上了年纪的人）”。

sentences.en: Basically, euphemisms help people talk about difficult topics like death, money, sex, or politics, in a softer and more socially acceptable way.
sentences.zh: 基本上，委婉语以一种更温和、更易于社会接受的方式，帮助人们谈论死亡、金钱、性或政治等敏感话题。

sentences.en: They are a way to be polite in social settings, and because politeness and sensitivity are cultural things (what is considered polite or rude differs between cultures) euphemisms reflect cultural attitudes about what is considered appropriate or respectful to say in public.
sentences.zh: 它们是在社交场合中保持礼貌的一种方式，而且由于礼貌和敏感度因文化而异（什么被认为是礼貌或粗鲁在不同文化中有所不同），委婉语反映了公众认为哪些言论得体或尊重的文化态度。

sentences.en: In some cultures, being too direct can sometimes sound rude or insensitive, so euphemisms are a way to avoid confrontation or embarrassment or discomfort.
sentences.zh: 在某些文化中，过于直接有时听起来很粗鲁或缺乏同理心，所以委婉语是避免对抗、尴尬或不适的一种方式。

sentences.en: They can also make your language sound more professional or diplomatic, which is why they’re so common in workplaces and news reports and politics.
sentences.zh: 它们还能让你的语言听起来更专业或更有外交辞令感，这就是为什么它们在职场、新闻报道和政治中如此常见。

sentences.en: For example, governments and companies often use euphemisms to make serious or negative things sound less harsh.
sentences.zh: 例如，政府和公司经常使用委婉语来让严肃或负面的事情听起来不那么刺耳。

sentences.en: The military might say “collateral damage” instead of saying “civilian deaths “.
sentences.zh: 军方可能会说“collateral damage（附带损伤）”而不是说“civilian deaths（平民死亡）”。

sentences.en: A business, might talk about “downsizing” instead of saying “firing workers”.
sentences.zh: 企业可能会谈论“downsizing（精简人员）”而不是说“firing workers（解雇工人）”。

sentences.en: These expressions can make situations sound more neutral and less emotional.
sentences.zh: 这些表达可以使情况听起来更中立、情绪色彩更淡。

sentences.en: They also hide for truth or make something bad seem acceptable.
sentences.zh: 它们也掩盖了真相，或者让某些糟糕的事情看起来可以接受。

sentences.en: That’s why it’s important for English learners to understand euphemisms and to be aware of why they are used.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么英语学习者理解委婉语并意识到它们被使用的原因非常重要。

sentences.en: Euphemisms can show kindness, respect, and sensitivity.
sentences.zh: 委婉语可以表达善意、尊重和关怀。

sentences.en: For example, when talking about an illness someone has or a relative who has died or passed away.
sentences.zh: 例如，当谈到某人患有的疾病或已经去世的亲人时。

sentences.en: And euphemisms can also be used to manipulate you, mislead you, or soften reality.
sentences.zh: 但委婉语也可以用来操纵你、误导你或粉饰现实。

sentences.en: When a company tells you they need to downsize, they really mean they’re going to fire you.
sentences.zh: 当一家公司告诉你他们需要精简人员时，他们的真实意思是要开除你。

sentences.en: There is also something called a dysphemism, which functions as the opposite of a euphemism.
sentences.zh: 还有一种东西叫做反委婉语（dysphemism），它的功能与委婉语相反。

sentences.en: Unlike euphemisms, dysphemisms do not seek to soften the harshness of the subject, but rather to emphasize the harshness.
sentences.zh: 与委婉语不同，反委婉语并不试图缓和主题的严厉性，而是去强调这种严厉性。

sentences.en: An example would be when someone says, “this food tastes like garbage”.
sentences.zh: 一个例子就是当有人说：“这食物尝起来像垃圾”。

sentences.en: Does it really taste like garbage? Probably not.
sentences.zh: 它真的尝起来像垃圾吗？可能不是。

sentences.en: But the word garbage is used to emphasize the negative feeling towards the food.
sentences.zh: 但使用“垃圾”这个词是为了强调对这种食物的负面感受。

sentences.en: In summary, euphemisms are used as substitutes for direct or potentially offensive words.
sentences.zh: 总之，委婉语被用作直接或潜在冒犯性词汇的替代品。

sentences.en: They let us be more polite and perhaps gentle in our words.
sentences.zh: 它们让我们在言语上更加礼貌，或许也更温和。

sentences.en: Finally, let’s talk briefly about slang.
sentences.zh: 最后，我们简单聊聊俚语。

sentences.en: Slang is perhaps the most creative part of a language, and it’s also constantly changing and evolving.
sentences.zh: 俚语可能是一门语言中最具有创造力的部分，而且它一直在变化和发展。

sentences.en: This makes it annoying and confusing to teach.
sentences.zh: 这使得教学变得令人烦恼且困惑。

sentences.en: The slang I grew up using is now totally irrelevant.
sentences.zh: 我长大的时候使用的俚语现在已经完全过时了。

sentences.en: Slang refers to very informal words and expressions that are usually used by particular groups of people.
sentences.zh: 俚语指的是非常非正式的词语和表达，通常由特定的群体使用。

sentences.en: For example, young people, online communities or people in certain professions will have different slang words.
sentences.zh: 例如，年轻人、网络社群或特定行业的人会有不同的俚语词汇。

sentences.en: Slang is the kind of language you’ll hear used among friends or social media or in pop culture or music.
sentences.zh: 俚语是你在朋友之间、社交媒体、流行文化或音乐中听到的一种语言。

sentences.en: For instance, you might hear someone say a party was “lit “, meaning amazing or exciting.
sentences.zh: 比如，你可能会听到有人说某个派对很“lit”，意思是太棒了或令人兴奋。

sentences.en: That someone “ghosted” them (suddenly stopped replying to messages).
sentences.zh: 某人“ghosted”了他们（突然不回复消息了）。

sentences.en: Or that they’re feeling “salty”, meaning bitter or angry.
sentences.zh: 或者他们感到“salty”，意思是苦涩或生气。

sentences.en: You might even hear “no cap”, which basically means I’m not lying or I’m serious.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可能会听到“no cap”，这基本上意味着我没有撒谎或者我很认真。

sentences.en: If I sound slightly unnatural or awkward using those slang terms, it’s because it is unnatural.
sentences.zh: 如果我使用这些俚语时听起来有点不自然或尴尬，那是因为它们本来就不自然。

sentences.en: I had to search online for common slang terms used today because I don’t really use much slang in my English, and I especially don’t use contemporary slang in my daily vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 我不得不上网搜索今天常用的俚语词汇，因为我在英语中其实不太使用俚语，而且我的日常词汇中尤其不使用当代俚语。

sentences.en: What makes slang interesting and frustrating is how fast it changes.
sentences.zh: 让俚语既有趣又令人沮丧的是它变化的速度之快。

sentences.en: A word that’s popular today might sound completely outdated next year.
sentences.zh: 今天流行的词，明年可能听起来就完全过时了。

sentences.en: Think about how words like groovy, cool or rad have come and gone over the past decades.
sentences.zh: 想想过去几十年里，groovy、cool或rad这样的词是如何来来去去的。

sentences.en: Today’s TikTok slang might disappear just as quickly as groovy has.
sentences.zh: 今天的TikTok俚语可能会像groovy一样迅速消失。

sentences.en: Slang is connected to identity and belonging.
sentences.zh: 俚语与身份认同和归属感息息相关。

sentences.en: It helps people show their part of a group.
sentences.zh: 它帮助人们展示自己属于某个群体。

sentences.en: Using the same slang as your friends or your colleagues, helps you fit in and express who you are.
sentences.zh: 使用和你的朋友或同事相同的俚语，能帮你融入其中并表达真实的自我。

sentences.en: It’s also a way to sound more casual. Sometimes slang is even used as a kind of rebellion against formal or traditional language.
sentences.zh: 这也是一种让语气更休闲的方式。有时俚语甚至被用作对正式或传统语言的一种叛逆。

sentences.en: For english learners, slang can be both exciting and challenging.
sentences.zh: 对于英语学习者来说，俚语既令人兴奋又充满挑战。

sentences.en: There’s new slang all the time, especially online.
sentences.zh: 新的俚语层出不穷，尤其是在网络上。

sentences.en: Memes, music and internet culture creates and spreads new words incredibly quickly.
sentences.zh: 表情包、音乐和网络文化以极其迅速的速度创造和传播着新词。

sentences.en: And slang isn’t universal. It changes depending on place.
sentences.zh: 而且俚语不是通用的。它会根据地点而变化。

sentences.en: The country or even the town you are in.
sentences.zh: 你所在的国家甚至城镇。

sentences.en: Your age, your social class, your hobbies.
sentences.zh: 你的年龄、你的社会阶层、你的爱好。

sentences.en: For example, “mate” and “cheers” are common in British slang; while “dude” or “awesome” are more American; Australians might say “arvo” for afternoon or “no worries” instead of your welcome.
sentences.zh: 例如，“mate”和“cheers”在英式俚语中很常见；而“dude”或“awesome”则更偏美式；澳大利亚人可能会用“arvo”表示下午，或者用“no worries”代替不客气。

sentences.en: Because slang changes so fast, it’s important to approach it with both curiosity and some caution.
sentences.zh: 由于俚语变化太快，以好奇和谨慎的态度来对待它是很重要的。

sentences.en: Understanding some slang might help you follow conversations or TV shows, but if you are thinking about using slang yourself, then you need an advanced sense of timing, context, and a lot of confidence.
sentences.zh: 理解一些俚语可能会帮你听懂对话或电视剧，但如果你考虑自己使用俚语，那么你需要具备高级的时机感、语境意识以及极大的自信。

sentences.en: Now that we’ve talked about what idioms, euphemisms, and slang are… should english learners like you spend your valuable time learning them?
sentences.zh: 既然我们已经讨论了什么是习语、委婉语和俚语……像你这样的英语学习者应该把宝贵的时间花在学习它们上面吗？

sentences.en: And if so, how much time or energy should you invest?
sentences.zh: 如果是的话，你应该投入多少时间和精力？

sentences.en: The short answer is… yes, it’s probably worth spending some time studying idioms and euphemisms, maybe slang, but in no way are they the most important part of English.
sentences.zh: 简短的回答是……是的，花点时间学习习语和委婉语可能是值得的，俚语或许也可以，但它们绝不是英语中最最重要的部分。

sentences.en: Of course, these types of expressions are a part of how native speakers actually communicate, so understanding them will make your listening and reading comprehension much stronger.
sentences.zh: 当然，这些类型的表达是母语者实际交流方式的一部分，所以理解它们会大大增强你的听说和阅读理解能力。

sentences.en: However, using them yourself is a completely different and often unnecessary skill.
sentences.zh: 然而，你自己去使用它们则是完全不同且通常不必要的技能。

sentences.en: Let’s start with the difference between recognition and production.
sentences.zh: 让我们从“识别”和“输出”的区别开始。

sentences.en: Your first goal should be recognition. Understanding what idioms, euphemisms, and slang mean when you hear them and read them.
sentences.zh: 你的首要目标应该是识别。当你听到和读到习语、委婉语和俚语时，理解它们是什么意思。

sentences.en: This helps you follow real life English: TV shows, podcasts, movies, conversations.
sentences.zh: 这能帮你跟上现实生活中的英语：电视剧、播客、电影、对话。

sentences.en: But you need to be really careful. Idioms and slang can easily sound unnatural, outdated, or inappropriate, offensive, if you use them in the wrong situation or with the wrong people.
sentences.zh: 但你必须非常小心。如果你在错误的场合或对错误的人使用习语和俚语，它们很容易听起来不自然、过时、不得体或具有攻击性。

sentences.en: Of course you can practice using an idiom in a conversation, maybe one of my conversation clubs, but be careful if you are out in the real world in a business meeting and you choose to use a slang term or an idiom.
sentences.zh: 当然，你可以在对话中练习使用习语，比如在我的聊天俱乐部里，但如果你身处现实世界的商务会议中，却选择使用某个俚语或习语，就要小心了。

sentences.en: Because maybe it’s the wrong situation, maybe it’s the wrong context.
sentences.zh: 因为可能场合不对，语境不对。

sentences.en: Maybe it makes you seem strange. When it comes to idioms, focus on comprehension first.
sentences.zh: 这或许会让你显得很奇怪。说到习语，首先要专注于理解。

sentences.en: You don’t need to memorize hundreds of idioms or try to use idioms all the time.
sentences.zh: 你不需要背诵几百个习语，也不需要时刻尝试使用习语。

sentences.en: I don’t really use idioms that much in my English, but when I do, I do it accidentally.
sentences.zh: 我在英语中其实不怎么用习语，但当我用的时候，都是无意中说出来的。

sentences.en: Like all native speakers, I use idioms naturally without thinking about it.
sentences.zh: 像所有母语者一样，我很自然地使用习语，根本不需要思考。

sentences.en: If you use too many idioms, it sounds strange or forced.
sentences.zh: 如果你用了太多习语，听起来会很奇怪或很勉强。

sentences.en: If you are thinking about using idioms, it sounds awkward.
sentences.zh: 如果你刻意去想怎么用习语，听起来就会很尴尬。

sentences.en: Start by recognizing common and widely understood idioms.
sentences.zh: 从识别常见且被广泛理解的习语开始。

sentences.en: Maybe like “under the weather” for meaning feeling sick.
sentences.zh: 比如用“under the weather”来表示感觉身体不舒服。

sentences.en: If you do want to use idioms in your own speech, stick to the simple and universal idioms that can naturally fit into your sentences.
sentences.zh: 如果你确实想在自己的发言中使用习语，请坚持使用那些简单、通用且能自然融入句子的习语。

sentences.en: Or maybe look for idioms or jargon terms that are often used in your industry.
sentences.zh: 或者寻找在你所在的行业中经常使用的习语或行话。

sentences.en: If you work in sales and you work with English speaking colleagues, they use a lot of strange sales idioms, business idioms, so maybe you should look those ones up specifically.
sentences.zh: 如果你从事销售工作，并且与说英语的同事共事，他们会使用很多奇怪的销售习语、商业习语，所以你可能需要专门去查阅这些。

sentences.en: Euphemisms, on the other hand, are genuinely useful to learn.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，委婉语是真正值得学习的。

sentences.en: Euphemisms are important. Especially for formal or professional communication.
sentences.zh: 委婉语很重要。特别是对于正式或专业的沟通。

sentences.en: Understanding euphemisms will help you read the news, read company statements, or understand political speeches more critically.
sentences.zh: 理解委婉语将帮助你更具批判性地阅读新闻、公司声明或理解政治演讲。

sentences.en: In workplaces, they can help you sound more polite and diplomatic.
sentences.zh: 在职场中，它们可以帮助你显得更礼貌、更有外交辞令。

sentences.en: For example, saying someone was “let go “rather than fired, or that a company is “restructuring” instead of cutting jobs, can make your language sound more professional and tactful.
sentences.zh: 例如，说某人被“let go”而不是被开除，或者说公司在“restructuring（重组）”而不是在削减岗位，能让你的语言听起来更专业、更得体。

sentences.en: And in your personal life, knowing euphemisms can avoid some awkward moments.
sentences.zh: 在你的个人生活中，了解委婉语可以避免一些尴尬的时刻。

sentences.en: Really out of the three things I’ve talked about today, euphemisms are the most important for you to know and the most useful for you to use.
sentences.zh: 说实话，在我今天谈到的这三类东西中，委婉语对你来说是最重要的，也是最实用的。

sentences.en: You don’t need to use slang. You don’t need to use idioms.
sentences.zh: 你不需要使用俚语。你不需要使用习语。

sentences.en: Really, I recommend not studying them. Euphemisms should be something you learn at least to recognize.
sentences.zh: 真的，我建议不要去刻意学习它们。委婉语至少应该成为你需要学会识别的东西。

sentences.en: Especially if you are working in a company and you need to use English to talk to employees who work for you.
sentences.zh: 特别是如果你在一家公司工作，需要用英语与向你汇报的员工交谈。

sentences.en: Slang is probably the trickiest thing for learners to use.
sentences.zh: 俚语可能是学习者最难使用的东西。

sentences.en: It’s fun, creative, but it’s very regional, very dependent on hobby or age or social class, and it’s fast changing.
sentences.zh: 它很有趣、很有创意，但它非常具有地域性，高度依赖于爱好、年龄或社会阶层，而且变化极快。

sentences.en: What sounds “cool” to one generation in one country might sound strange or weird in another place.
sentences.zh: 在一个国家的某一世代听起来很“酷”的词，在另一个地方可能会显得很奇怪或古怪。

sentences.en: So my advice is to avoid using too much slang yourself unless you are sure it fits the situation.
sentences.zh: 所以我给出的建议是：除非你确信它符合语境，否则尽量避免自己使用太多俚语。

sentences.en: If you are talking with friends who are your own age, a bit of slang can sound natural, but in professional or academic settings, it’s usually best to not use slang.
sentences.zh: 如果你在和同龄的朋友聊天，用一点俚语听起来可能很自然，但在专业或学术场合，最好还是不要使用俚语。

sentences.en: It’s usually best to keep things more neutral.
sentences.zh: 保持语言更加中立通常是最好的选择。

sentences.en: The best way to learn idioms, euphemisms, and slang, is through context.
sentences.zh: 学习习语、委婉语和俚语的最佳方式是通过语境。

sentences.en: Don’t memorize lists. Instead, notice them in movies, podcasts, YouTube videos, conversations that you have.
sentences.zh: 不要去背诵列表。相反，要在电影、播客、YouTube视频、你进行的对话中去注意它们。

sentences.en: Pay attention to who uses them, when they are used, and how they are used.
sentences.zh: 留心是谁在用、什么时候用以及如何使用的。

sentences.en: This is why I don’t really like YouTube videos or Instagram videos that introduce idioms by themselves with no context, because it doesn’t help you know when to use them.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我其实不太喜欢那些脱离语境孤立介绍习语的YouTube或Instagram视频，因为这无助于你了解何时使用它们。

sentences.en: It doesn’t help you understand really anything about the idiom.
sentences.zh: 这无助于你真正理解关于这个习语的任何实质内容。

sentences.en: Perhaps when you hear me use an idiom in this episode or when you hear in a TV show someone use a slang term you’ve not heard before, you can make a note of it and mark whether it is used in a casual way, a polite way, a formal way.
sentences.zh: 也许当你在这一期节目中听到我使用某个习语，或者当你在电视剧里听到别人使用你从未听过的俚语时，你可以把它记下来，并标注它是用于日常随意的场合、礼貌的场合，还是正式的场合。

sentences.en: Over time, you will develop a natural sense of what’s appropriate or what’s not appropriate.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，你将对什么得体、什么不得体培养出一种自然的语感。

sentences.en: Basically understanding, comprehension, needs to come before usage.
sentences.zh: 基本上，理解必须先于使用。

sentences.en: Focus on recognizing expressions first, and then as your English grows, you might start to feel comfortable using some euphemisms, some idioms, some slang yourself.
sentences.zh: 先专注于识别各种表达，然后随着你的英语水平不断提高，你可能会开始觉得可以自如地使用一些委婉语、习语甚至俚语了。

sentences.en: Just to quickly summarize… An idiom is a phrase whose meaning isn’t literal, like “break the ice” or “spill the beans “.
sentences.zh: 简单快速地总结一下……习语是一个字面意思与实际含义不同的短语，比如“break the ice”或“spill the beans”。

sentences.en: A euphemism is a polite or indirect way to talk about something uncomfortable, like “passed away” instead of died.
sentences.zh: 委婉语是谈论某些令人不适的事情时一种礼貌或间接的方式，比如用“passed away”代替“died”。

sentences.en: And slang is very informal, often trendy language used by specific groups, like “lit” or “ghosted “.
sentences.zh: 而俚语是非常非正式的、通常很时髦的语言，由特定群体使用，比如“lit”或“ghosted”。

sentences.en: Each of these things makes English sound more natural and expressive, but they can also be confusing or risky to use.
sentences.zh: 这些元素中的每一个都让英语听起来更自然、更有表现力，但使用它们也可能令人困惑或带有风险。

sentences.en: You don’t need to use them at all, but understanding them will help you follow real conversations, media and culture more easily.
sentences.zh: 你根本不需要使用它们，但理解它们将帮助你更轻松地跟上真实的对话、媒体和文化。

sentences.en: Focus on recognizing them first, and over time you’ll naturally learn when and how to use them yourself.
sentences.zh: 先专注于识别它们，随着时间的推移，你自然会学会何时以及如何亲自使用它们。

sentences.en: Specifically, if you are going to take one thing from this episode, it’s that euphemisms are probably the most important thing to understand and learn how to use, followed by some idioms, especially professional idioms used in your industry.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，如果你要从这期节目中带走一件事，那就是委婉语可能是最重要、最需要理解和学会使用的，其次是一些习语，尤其是你所在行业中使用的专业习语。

sentences.en: What do you think? Do you try to use idioms, euphemisms, or slang in your English?
sentences.zh: 你怎么看？你在英语中尝试过使用习语、委婉语或俚语吗？

sentences.en: What are some interesting or common slang terms or idioms from your language, from your country?
sentences.zh: 你的语言、你的国家有哪些有趣或常见的俚语或习语呢？
